title: Lemma
body_md:
\label[Lemma]{lem:Lindbladian_properties}
The Lindbladian $\mathcal{L}$ defined in
\eqref{eq:Lindbladian_unparametric} is a linear operator
$\mathcal{L}:\mathcal H\to A_0$ and satisfies
$(\ker\mathcal{L})\cap S\neq\emptyset$
and 
$\ker\mathcal{L}
=
\operatorname{span}_{\ensuremath\mathbb{R}}\bigl((\ker\mathcal{L})\cap S\bigr).$

In particular, the steady-state problem, 
i.e., finding $\rho_{\mathrm{ss}} \in S$ such that $\mathcal{L}\rho_{\mathrm{ss}} = 0$,
has a solution in~$S$,
and a solution is unique if and only if $\dim\ker\mathcal{L}=1$.
head: environment
name: Basic properties of Lindbladians

title: Proof
body_md:
Linearity, Hermiticity preservation and
$\operatorname{tr}(\mathcal{L} X)=0$ follow directly from
\eqref{eq:Lindbladian_unparametric}. 
The existence of stationary states 
and the relation $\ker\mathcal{L}
=
\operatorname{span}_{\ensuremath\mathbb{R}}\bigl((\ker\mathcal{L})\cap S\bigr)$
for finite-dimensional GKSL generators
are established in~\cite[Sec.~3.6 and~4.1]{BaumgartnerNarnhofer2008}. 
The final assertion follows from $\ker\mathcal{L}
=
\operatorname{span}_{\ensuremath\mathbb{R}}\bigl((\ker\mathcal{L})\cap S\bigr)$ and the trace-one
normalization; see also \cite[Sec.~3.6 and~4.1]{BaumgartnerNarnhofer2008}.
head: environment
name: Proof sketch

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label[lemma]{lem:geometric_properties}
It holds that
\[
\mathcal H=A_0\oplus\operatorname{span}_{\ensuremath\mathbb{R}}\{I\},
\qquad
A_1
=
{I}/{N}
+A_0,
\qquad
S=A_1\cap\mathcal H_+.
\]
In particular, $A_1$ is an affine convex subset of $\mathcal H$,
$S$ is a compact convex subset of $\mathcal H$, and
\[
{1}/{\sqrt N} \leq \|X\|  
\quad\text{for }X\in A_1,
\qquad
{1}/{\sqrt N}\leq\|\rho\|\leq1
\quad\text{for }\rho\in S.
\]
head: environment
name: Basic geometric properties

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\langle X,I\rangle=\operatorname{tr} X$, we have
$A_0=\operatorname{span}_{\ensuremath\mathbb{R}}\{I\}^{\perp}$, and every $X\in A_1$ has the unique
representation $X=I/N+X_0$ with $X_0\in A_0$. Moreover,
$1=\langle X,I\rangle\leq\sqrt N\|X\|$ for $X\in A_1$. If
$\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_N\geq0$ are the eigenvalues of $\rho\in S$, then
$\sum_i\lambda_i=1$ and
$1/N\leq\|\rho\|^2=\sum_i\lambda_i^2\leq1$. Finally,
$S=A_1\cap\mathcal H_+$ is closed and convex, and its boundedness together
with finite dimensionality gives compactness.
head: environment

label: eq:steady_state_eqn_as_LES
title: Remark
body_md:
\label[Remark]{rem:steady_state_eqn_as_LES}
By \Cref{lem:geometric_properties}, every
$\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}\in S$ can be written uniquely 
as $\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}=I/N+X$ with $X\in A_0$. 
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
\mathcal{L}\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}=0
\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
\mathcal{L} X
=
- 
N^{-1}
\mathcal{L} I.
\label{eq:steady_state_eqn_as_LES}
\end{equation}
Therefore, the steady-state problem on $A_1$ is
equivalently an inhomogeneous linear equation on~$A_0$.

name: Affine decomposition structure

title: Definition
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label[lemma]{lem:linear_affine_widths_equivalent}
For $n\geq0$, define the affine Kolmogorov-$n$-width by 
\[
d_n^{\mathrm{aff}}(\mathcal M)
\coloneqq
\inf_{\substack{V\subseteq\mathcal H,\,\dim V\leq n\\X_0\in\mathcal H}}
\sup_{\rho\in\mathcal M}\mathrm{dist}(\rho,X_0+V).
\]
Then it holds that 
\(
d_{n+1}(\mathcal M)
\leq d_n^{\mathrm{aff}}(\mathcal M)
\leq d_n(\mathcal M).
\)
head: environment
name: Linear and affine widths

title: Proof
body_md:
The upper bound follows by choosing $X_0=0$. 
For the lower bound, 
$X_0+V$ is contained in $\operatorname{span}_{\ensuremath\mathbb{R}}(\{X_0\}\cup V)$, 
whose dimension is at most $n+1$.
head: environment

title: Assumption
body_md:
We assume access to a solver which, 
for every selected $\mu\in\mathcal{P}$, 
yields a $\rho_\mu$, 
such that $\mathrm{dist} \big(\rho_\mu, S \cap\ker \mathcal{L}(\mu) \big)$ is below any prescribed numerical accuracy.
We denote $\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu) \coloneqq \rho_\mu$, 
and regard it as an \emph{exact steady state}.
head: environment
name: Steady-state solver

title: Remark
body_md:
\label[remark]{rem:RBM_pLindblad_outline} 
Given a parametric Lindbladian $\mathcal{L}(\mu)$ as in \Cref{ass:affine_decomp_param_Lindbladian},
the RB procedure consists of the following two phases: 
\begin{itemize}
\item 
The \emph{offline phase} assembles a reduced space $V$ based on snapshot solutions $\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu_1),\dots, \rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu_J)$.
Common assembly strategies include \emph{proper orthogonal decomposition (POD)},
or \emph{greedy methods}, see \Cref{subsubsec:POD_vs_greedy}.
Once $V$ is constructed, 
with an orthonormal basis (ONB) $B_1, \dots,  B_r$ available,
we compute and store parameter-independent quantities \eqref{eq:offline_HH_matrix}--\eqref{eq:offline_DD_matrix},
which will be used for reduced approximation of the steady states.
\item 
In the \emph{online phase}, given any $\mu \in \mathcal{P}$,
we assemble the reduced model \eqref{eq:online_assembly_reduced_normal_matrix}, 
choose a reduced formulation \eqref{eq:abstract_EVP} or \eqref{eq:abstract_constraint_res_min}, 
compute a corresponding reduced solution 
$\rho_{\mathrm{eig}}^{(r)}(\mu)$ or $\rho_{\mathrm{aff}}^{(r)}(\mu)$ 
as specified later in \eqref{eq:trace_normalized_reduced_eigenvector} or \eqref{eq:reduced_affine_approximation}, respectively.
The resulting approximation is Hermitian. 
It has unit trace in the affine
formulation \eqref{eq:abstract_constraint_res_min} and, 
provided that the trace normalization is well-defined, also
in the eigenvalue formulation \eqref{eq:abstract_EVP}.
Post-processing procedures for positivity, 
as described in \Cref{subsec:post_processing}, 
can be optionally performed. 
\end{itemize}
head: environment
name: RBM for parametric Lindbladian

label: rem:observable
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:observable}
For an observable $O \in \mathcal{H}$, 
one is interested in {its expectation value with respect to the steady state $\rho(\mu)$},
i.e.,
\[
\langle O\rangle_{\rho(\mu)}
\coloneqq
\langle O,\rho(\mu)\rangle
=
\operatorname{tr}\bigl(O\rho(\mu)\bigr),
\]
for different parameters $\mu\in\mathcal{P}$.
Let $V$ be an offline-constructed reduced space, 
with ONB $B_1,\ldots,B_r$. 
For $\star\in\{\mathrm{eig},\mathrm{aff}\}$, 
let $x_\star^{(r)}(\mu)$ denote the coefficient vector 
of $\rho_\star^{(r)}(\mu)$ in this basis.
Once $O$ is supplied, 
its reduced representation $o_r
\coloneqq
(
\langle O,B_1\rangle,\ldots,\langle O,B_r\rangle
)^\top$ is computed once, 
and the expectation is evaluated as
\[
\langle O\rangle_{\rho_\star^{(r)}(\mu)}
\, = \, 
o_r^\top x_\star^{(r)}(\mu).
\]
Thus, for the evaluation of the observable $O$,
only the one-time construction of~$o_r$ involves full-order quantities.
Subsequent parameter queries require no state reconstruction or other full-order computations,
unless positivity postprocessing is applied.
head: environment
name: Reduced evaluation of observables

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label[lemma]{prop:projection_postprocessing_error}
For $\rho\in A_1$ and
$\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)\in S$,
it holds that 
\begin{equation*}
\left\|
\Pi_S(\rho)
-
\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)
\right\| 
\leq
\left\|
\rho-\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)
\right\| .
\end{equation*}
head: environment
name: Error after projection onto the state set

title: Proof
body_md:
Metric projections onto a nonempty closed convex subset 
of a Hilbert space are nonexpansive 
by \cite[Prp.~4.8]{BauschkeCombettes2017}.
Hence, for $\Pi_S$ from \Cref{subsubsec:metric_proj} and $S$ convex,
we have $\|\Pi_S(X)-\Pi_S(Y)\|\leq\|X-Y\|$ for all $X,Y\in\mathcal{H}$. 
With $\Pi_S\bigl(\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)\bigr) = \rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu) \in S$,
the assertion follows.
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label[lemma]{prop:partial_clipping_error}
Let $\rho\in A_1$, $\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)\in S$, 
and $\Pi_{\mathrm{clip},k}(\rho)$ the partially clipped approximation from
\eqref{eq:partial_clipping_map}. 
Then, it holds that 
\begin{equation*}
\left\|
\Pi_{\mathrm{clip},k}(\rho)
-
\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)
\right\| 
\, \leq \, 
\bigl(2+\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{clip}}}\bigr)
\left\|
\rho-\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)
\right\| ,
\end{equation*}
where $n_{\mathrm{clip}} $
 is the number of actually clipped eigenvalues, 
i.e.,
\begin{equation*}
n_{\mathrm{clip}} 
\coloneqq
\operatorname{rank} C_k(\rho)
=
\operatorname{card}
\bigl\{
j\in\{N-k+1,\ldots,N\}:
\lambda_j<0
\bigr\} 
\leq k.
\end{equation*}
head: environment
name: Error after partial spectral clipping

title: Proof
body_md:
For brevity, set
$C_k\coloneqq C_k(\rho)$,
$s_k\coloneqq s_k(\rho)$ 
and
$E\coloneqq\rho-\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)$.
Let $\mu_1\geq\cdots\geq\mu_N\geq0$ denote the eigenvalues of
$\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)$. Since
$\max\{-\lambda_j,0\}\leq|\lambda_j-\mu_j|$,
the Hoffman--Wielandt inequality
\cite[Thm.~6.3.5 and Cor.~6.3.8]{HornJohnson2012} yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|C_k\|^2
=
\sum_{j=N-k+1}^{N}
\max\{-\lambda_j,0\}^2 
\leq
\sum_{j=1}^{N}|\lambda_j-\mu_j|^2
\leq
\|E\|^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Moreover, $C_k$ is positive semidefinite and has rank
$n_{\mathrm{clip}}$. 
Hence, we have 
\[
s_k
=
\operatorname{tr} C_k
\leq
\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{clip}}}\,\|C_k\|
\leq
\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{clip}}}\,\|E\|.
\]
Finally, using \eqref{eq:partial_clipping_map},
$\|\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)\|\leq1$ and $1+s_k\geq1$, we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left\|
\Pi_{\mathrm{clip},k}(\rho)-\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)
\right\|
=
\frac{
\left\|E+C_k-s_k\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)\right\|
}{1+s_k} 
\leq
\|E\|+\|C_k\|+s_k\|\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)\| 
\leq
\bigl(2+\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{clip}}}\bigr)\|E\|,
\end{aligned}
\]
which proves the assertion.
head: environment

label: eq:beta_gamma_angle_rel
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Gap--angle bound for trace-zero stability

title: Proof
body_md:
For $X\in A_0$, decompose $X = X_{\parallel} + X_{\perp}$ 
with $X_{\parallel} \in \ker\mathcal{L}(\mu)$ and $X_{\perp} \in \ker\mathcal{L}(\mu)^\perp$. 
Note that $\|\mathcal{L}(\mu)X\|^2 = \langle X_\perp, \mathcal{A}(\mu)X_\perp\rangle $.
Hence, the definition of $\gamma(\mu)$ and the minimal angle $\psi(\mu)$ in
\eqref{eq:gap_and_trace_zero_stability} give
\[
\|\mathcal{L}(\mu)X\|^2
\geq
\gamma(\mu)
\operatorname{dist}\bigl(X,\ker\mathcal{L}(\mu)\bigr)^2
\geq
\gamma(\mu)\, \sin^2\!\psi(\mu)\, \|X\|^2.
\]
Taking the minimum over $X\in A_0$ with $\|X\|=1$ proves \eqref{eq:beta_gamma_angle_rel}.


In the unique steady-state case, 
we set $u \coloneqq \rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu) / \|\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)\|$
and observe that 
$\ker\mathcal{L}(\mu)  
= \operatorname{span}\{\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)\}
= \operatorname{span} \{u\}$.
Using this fact and $\|u\|=1$,
we deduce that 
$$
\sin^2\!\psi(\mu)
=
\inf_{\substack{X\in A_0\\\|X\|=1}}
\mathrm{dist}(X, \ker \mathcal{L}(\mu))^2
=
\inf_{\substack{X\in A_0\\\|X\|=1}}
1- |\langle X,u\rangle|^2
=
1- \sup_{\substack{X\in A_0\\\|X\|=1}}
|\langle X,u\rangle|^2.
$$ 
Moreover, 
observe that 
$\sup_{\substack{X\in A_0,\|X\|=1}}
|\langle X,u\rangle|^2
= \|P_{A_0}u\|^2
$,
where $P_{A_0}$ is the orthogonal projector onto $A_0$.
Hence, by setting 
$n \coloneqq I / \sqrt{N}$,
which satisfies $n \perp A_0$, 
we obtain 
$1-\|P_{A_0}u\|^2 = |\langle u, n \rangle|^2$.
Combining these considerations and using $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)=1$,
we see that 
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sin^2\!\psi(\mu)
=
1- \sup_{\substack{X\in A_0\\\|X\|=1}}
|\langle X,u\rangle|^2
=
1-\|P_{A_0}u\|^2  
=
|\langle u,n\rangle|^2
=
\frac{1}{N\|\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)\|^2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The rest follows from $\|\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)\|\in [1/\sqrt{N},1]$;
see \Cref{lem:geometric_properties}.
head: environment

title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Residual-based state-error estimate

title: Proof
body_md:
Set $E
\coloneqq
\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)
-{X}/{\operatorname{tr} X}
.$
Since both terms have unit trace, $E\in A_0$.  
The definition of
$\beta(\mu)$ and $\mathcal{L}(\mu)\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)=0$ 
give
$\beta(\mu)\|E\|
\leq
\|\mathcal{L}(\mu)E\|
=
{\|\mathcal{L}(\mu)X\|}/{|\operatorname{tr} X|},$
which proves the claim.

title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Weak greedy convergence rates for RBM

title: Remark
body_md:
\label[remark]{rem:fixed_initial_space_weak_greedy}
The standard weak greedy theorem is commonly formulated for a sequence starting from the zero space.
The formulation above also covers an arbitrary fixed initial space~$V_1$.
To see this, 
let $P_1^\perp$ be the orthogonal projector onto $V_1^\perp$ and 
set $\tilde{\mathcal M}\coloneqq P_1^\perp\mathcal M$.
For every space $V_r$ containing~$V_1$, we have
\begin{equation*}
\mathrm{dist}(u(\mu),V_r)
=
\mathrm{dist}\bigl(P_1^\perp u(\mu),P_1^\perp V_r\bigr)
\qquad \text{and} \qquad
d_n(\tilde{\mathcal M})
\leq
d_n(\mathcal M).
\end{equation*}
Hence, the standard theorem can be applied to the projected greedy sequence in~$V_1^\perp$.
This explains the index shift on the left hand side of  \eqref{eq:weak_greedy_exponential_rate}.
head: environment
name: Fixed initial reduced space

label: lem:error_equivalence_weak_greedy
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:error_equivalence_weak_greedy}
For each $r\in \mathbb{N}$, suppose there exists $\Delta^{(r)}:\mathcal{P} \to [0,\infty)$,
such that 
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:indicator_projection_error_equivalence}
c \, \Delta^{(r)}(\mu)
\, \leq \,
\mathrm{dist}(u(\mu), V_r)^2
\, \leq \,
C \, \Delta^{(r)}(\mu)
\qquad \text{for all }
\mu \in \mathcal{P},
\end{equation} 
where $c,C>0$ are constants independent of $r$ and of $\mu$.
Then, the sequence $(\mu_r)_{r \in \mathbb{N}}$ selected via 
$\mu_r \, \in \, \operatorname*{arg\,max}_{\mu \in \mathcal{P}} \Delta^{(r)}(\mu)$
satisfies the
condition \Cref{thm:weak_greedy_convergence_rates}~\ref{item:weak_greedy} with $\vartheta = \sqrt{c / C} $.
head: environment
name: Error equivalence sufficient for weak greedy selection

title: Assumption
head: environment
name: Continuity and uniform well-posedness

label: lem:compact_solution_set
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:compact_solution_set}
Under \Cref{ass:continuous_wellposedness},
the solution map $u=\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}:\mathcal{P}\to\mathcal H$ is well-defined and continuous,
and the solution set $\mathcal M=\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mathcal{P})$ is compact.
head: environment
name: Sufficient condition for a compact solution set

title: Proof
body_md:
By \Cref{ass:affine_decomp_param_Lindbladian}
and \Cref{ass:continuous_wellposedness},
both $\mathcal{L}:\mathcal{P}\to\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ and
$\mathcal{L}_0:\mathcal{P}\to\mathcal B(A_0)$ are continuous.
Since inversion is continuous on the set of invertible operators,
\eqref{eq:steady_state_solution_map_formula} implies continuity of
$\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}:\mathcal{P}\to\mathcal H$.
Together with compactness of~$\mathcal{P}$,
we deduce compactness of $\mathcal M=\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mathcal{P})$.
head: environment

label: prp:valid_weak_greedy
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Efficient and reliable snapshot selection rules

title: Proof
body_md:
The claims on $\varrho_{\max}$ and $\gamma_{\min}$ follow from the
variational characterization and continuity of the ordered eigenvalues.
Continuity of the steady-state map from \Cref{lem:compact_solution_set} and
compactness of $\mathcal{P}$ show that $\nu_{\min}$ is attained; moreover,
$\nu_{\min}\geq1/N$ by \Cref{lem:geometric_properties}.  
Finally,
$\mathcal{L}_0(\mu)$ is continuously invertible 
under \Cref{ass:continuous_wellposedness} and
$\beta(\mu)
=
\|\mathcal{L}_0(\mu)^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{-1}$
with $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ denoting the operator norm. 
Thus, $\beta$ is continuous and strictly positive, 
and compactness of $\mathcal{P}$ yields
$\beta_{\min}>0$.  


Let us choose arbitrary $r\in \mathbb{N}$ and $\mu \in \mathcal{P}$. 
For brevity, we suppress the dependence on $\mu$ throughout the remainder of the proof and simply denote
\[
\mathcal L\coloneqq\mathcal{L}(\mu),
\qquad
\mathcal A\coloneqq\mathcal A(\mu),
\qquad
\rho\coloneqq\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu),
\qquad
u\coloneqq {\rho}/{\|\rho\|}.
\]
We also write
$\gamma, \rho_{\mathrm n}^{(r)}$, $\rho_{\mathrm{aff}}^{(r)}$,
$\Delta_{\mathrm{eig}}^{(r)}$ and $\Delta_{\mathrm{aff}}^{(r)}$
for the corresponding quantities at the chosen~$\mu$.


Let $P\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ and $P^\perp\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$
denote the orthogonal projectors onto $V_r$ and $V_r^\perp$, respectively.
In particular, $\mathrm{dist}(\rho,V_r)=\|P^\perp\rho\|$.
For any $X\in\mathcal H$, let $P_X$ denote the orthogonal projector onto
$\operatorname{span}_\mathbb R\{X\}$.
Observe that 
\begin{equation}
\|P_u X\|
\, = \,
\|P_{X} u\|
\, \leq \, 
\|P u\|
\qquad \text{for }
X \in V_r
\text{ with }\|X\|=1,
\label{eq:norm_interchange}
\end{equation}
with equality when $P u \in \operatorname{span}\{X\}$, 
i.e., when $Pu\neq 0$ and $X=\pm Pu/\|Pu\|$ 
due to the norm constraint for $X$. 
We also have 
$\ker\mathcal L=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{ \rho \}$ and  
\begin{equation}
\mathrm{dist}(X,\ker\mathcal L)^2 
=
\|P_u^\perp X\|^2 
=
1-\|P_u X\|^2
\qquad \text{for any }\|X\|=1.
\label{eq:normalized_projection_error_relation}
\end{equation}
Note that $\mathcal{A}P_{ u } = \mathcal{L}^\dagger \mathcal{L}P_{u }= 0$.
Hence, 
we use $X = P_{u } X + P_{u }^\perp X$ and the definition of $\gamma_{\min}$ to deduce 
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:gap_ker_dist_relation}
    \langle X, \mathcal A X\rangle
=
\langle P_{ u }^\perp X, \mathcal A P_{ u }^\perp X\rangle
\geq
\gamma_{\min} \|P_{ u }^\perp X\|^2
=
\gamma_{\min}\,
(1-\|P_u X\|^2)
\qquad \text{for any }\|X\|=1.
\end{equation}

\noindent $\bullet$ 
\emph{We now prove \ref{item:eig_formulation_error_equivalence}}. 
Consider $\rho^{(r)}_{\mathrm{n}}$ from \eqref{eq:norm_normalized_reduced_eigenvector}.
Note that 
$\Delta^{(r)}_\mathrm{eig} = \langle \rho^{(r)}_{\mathrm{n}}, \mathcal{A}\rho^{(r)}_{\mathrm{n}} \rangle$
and 
$\|\rho^{(r)}_{\mathrm{n}}\|=1$. 
For every $X\in V_r$ with $\|X\|=1$, 
\eqref{eq:gap_ker_dist_relation} 
and \eqref{eq:norm_interchange} yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
\langle X,\mathcal A X\rangle
\geq
\gamma_{\min}\big(1-\|P_u X\|^2\big)
\geq
\gamma_{\min}\big(1-\|P u\|^2\big)
=
\gamma_{\min}\mathrm{dist}(u,V_r)^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Applying this estimate to $\rho^{(r)}_{\mathrm n}$,
and using $\|\rho\|\leq1$ from
\Cref{lem:geometric_properties}, we obtain 
\[
\mathrm{dist}(\rho,V_r)^2
\leq
\mathrm{dist}(u,V_r)^2
\leq
\gamma_{\min}^{-1}
\Delta^{(r)}_{\mathrm{eig}}.
\]


To prove the first inequality,
note that $I\in V_r$ and
$\langle\rho,I\rangle=\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$.
Hence, $P\rho\neq0$,
and 
$ X_\rho \coloneqq P\rho/\|P\rho\| \in V_r$ is admissible in \eqref{eq:abstract_EVP}.
Applying \eqref{eq:norm_interchange} and
\eqref{eq:normalized_projection_error_relation},
we deduce
$$
\|P_u^\perp X_\rho\|^2
= 1-\|P_u X_\rho\|^2 = 1-\|P_{X_\rho }u\|^2
= 1-\|P u\|^2
= \mathrm{dist}(u,V_r)^2
= \|\rho\|^{-2} {\mathrm{dist}(\rho,V_r)^2}.
$$
Using 
the minimizing property of
$\rho_{\mathrm n}^{(r)}$, 
$ \mathcal{L} = \mathcal{L} P_u^\perp $, 
 the definitions of
$\varrho_{\max}$ and $\nu_{\min}$,
and the previous identity,
we obtain
\[
\Delta_{\mathrm{eig}}^{(r)}
\leq
\|\mathcal{L} X_\rho\|^2
= \|\mathcal{L} P_u^\perp X_\rho\|^2
\leq
\varrho_{\max}
\|P_u^\perp X_\rho\|^2
=
{\varrho_{\max}}{\|\rho\|^{-2}}\mathrm{dist}(\rho,V_r)^2
\leq
{\varrho_{\max}}\,{\nu_{\min}^{-1}}\,\mathrm{dist}(\rho,V_r)^2.
\]

\smallskip
\noindent $\bullet$ 
\emph{We now prove \ref{item:aff_formulation_error_equivalence}}. 
Consider $\rho^{(r)}_{\mathrm{aff}}$ from \eqref{eq:reduced_affine_approximation}.
Note that 
$\Delta^{(r)}_\mathrm{aff} = \|\mathcal L\rho^{(r)}_{\mathrm{aff}} \|^2$
and 
$\operatorname{tr} \rho^{(r)}_{\mathrm{aff}} =1$. 
As observed above, $P \rho\in V_r\cap A_1$ is admissible in
\eqref{eq:reduced_affine_residual_problem}. 
Hence, the minimizing property of $\varrho^{(r)}_{\mathrm{aff}}$,
$ \mathcal{L}\rho=0$, and the definition of $\rho_{\max}$ imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta^{(r)}_{\mathrm{aff}}
\leq
\|\mathcal L P \rho\|^2
=
\|\mathcal L(P \rho-\rho)\|^2
\leq
\varrho_{\max}\|P^\perp\rho\|^2
=
\varrho_{\max}\mathrm{dist}(\rho,V_r)^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves the first inequality in
\ref{item:aff_formulation_error_equivalence}. 

Finally, set
$E^{(r)}_{\mathrm{aff}}
\coloneqq
\rho^{(r)}_{\mathrm{aff}}-\rho$.
Since both matrices have unit trace, $E^{(r)}_{\mathrm{aff}}\in A_0$.
By the definitions of $\beta(\mu)$ and $\beta_{\min}$,
it holds that  $\Delta^{(r)}_{\mathrm{aff}}
=
\|\mathcal L E^{(r)}_{\mathrm{aff}}\|^2
\geq
\beta_{\min}^2\|E^{(r)}_{\mathrm{aff}}\|^2.$
Since $\rho^{(r)}_{\mathrm{aff}}\in V_r$, 
we have 
$\mathrm{dist}(\rho,V_r)^2
\leq \|\rho^{(r)}_{\mathrm{aff}}-\rho\|^2 
= 
\| E^{(r)}_{\mathrm{aff}} \|^2$.
Combining these two estimates 
yields the desired inequality.
head: environment

title: Assumption
head: environment
name: Real-analytic parameter dependence

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label[proposition]{prop:analyticity_steady_state_map}
Suppose \Cref{ass:continuous_wellposedness}
and \Cref{ass:real_analytic_parameter_dependence} hold.
Then the steady-state map
$\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}:\mathcal{P}\to\mathcal H$ is real-analytic,
in the sense that it admits an $\mathcal H$-valued real-analytic extension
to an open neighborhood $\Omega_0\subseteq\Omega$ of~$\mathcal{P}$.
head: environment
name: Analyticity of the steady-state map

title: Proof
body_md:
By \Cref{ass:real_analytic_parameter_dependence} and the affine decomposition
\eqref{eq:Lindbladian_affine_decomposition},
$\mathcal{L}$ admits a real-analytic extension to~$\Omega$,
which we denote again by~$\mathcal{L}$.
The definition of $\mathcal{L}_0$ from \eqref{eq:restricted_Lindbladian_A0}
extends to~$\Omega$ by the same restriction formula,
and the resulting operator-valued map is real-analytic.
By \Cref{ass:continuous_wellposedness} and \eqref{eq:equivalence_unique_steady_state},
$\mathcal{L}_0(\mu)$ is invertible for every $\mu\in\mathcal{P}$.
Since the set of invertible operators on~$A_0$ is open,
\(
\Omega_0
\coloneqq
\{
\mu\in\Omega:
\mathcal{L}_0(\mu)\text{ is invertible}
\}
\)
is an open neighborhood of~$\mathcal{P}$.

The inversion map is real-analytic on the set of invertible operators.
Hence, the right hand side of \eqref{eq:steady_state_solution_map_formula}
defines an $\mathcal H$-valued real-analytic map on~$\Omega_0$.
On~$\mathcal{P}$, it coincides with the steady-state map,
and therefore, provides the asserted extension.

label: eq:generalized_exponential_width_decay
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Exponential or sub-exponential width decay

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $T:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}^{d}$ be an affine bijection
satisfying $T([-1,1]^{d})=\mathcal{P}$,
and set $F\coloneqq\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}\circ T$.
By \Cref{prop:analyticity_steady_state_map},
$F$ is real-analytic on an open neighborhood of the compact cube
$[-1,1]^{d}$.
By the standard complexification result 
for finite-dimensional real-analytic maps, 
cf.~\cite[Sec.~2.2]{KrantzParks2002}, 
$F$ admits a holomorphic extension 
to a complex neighborhood of the cube, 
with values in 
$\mathcal H \otimes \mathbb{C} = \mathbb{C}^{N \times N}$.
Hence, after possibly reducing this neighborhood,
there exists $R>1$, 
such that this extension is bounded 
and holomorphic on the product Bernstein polyellipse $\mathcal E_R^{d} \subseteq \mathbb{C}^{d}$,
where $\mathcal E_R\subseteq\ensuremath\mathbb{C}$ denotes the Bernstein ellipse with parameter~$R$,
cf.~\cite[Sec.~2.2]{KrantzParks2002}.

For every integer $m\geq0$, 
let $\mathcal I_mF$ be the tensorized Chebyshev-Lobatto interpolant
of degree~$m$ in each parameter direction.
The standard interpolation estimate for functions that are holomorphic on a
Bernstein polyellipse gives
\begin{equation}
\sup_{y\in[-1,1]^{d}}
\|
F(y)-\mathcal I_mF(y)
\|
\,\leq\,
C_0R^{-m}
\label{eq:vector_chebyshev_interpolation_error}
\end{equation}
for some constant $C_0>0$ independent of~$m$;
see, e.g., \cite{NobileTamelliniTempone2016,ChkifaCohenSchwab2014,AdcockBrugiapagliaDexterMoraga2024}
for polynomial approximation and interpolation of Hilbert- or Banach-space-valued maps.

Let $(y_\nu)_{\nu\in\{0,\ldots,m\}^{d}}$ be the tensorized Chebyshev nodes.
The Lagrange representation of the interpolant
with respect to a Lagrangian basis 
$\{\ell_\nu\}_{\nu\in\{0,\ldots,m\}^d}$ 
reads
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal I_mF(y)
\, = \!
\sum_{\nu\in\{0,\ldots,m\}^{d}}
\ell_\nu(y)F(y_\nu).
\end{equation*}
Consequently, $\mathcal I_mF(y)$ belongs to the snapshot space
$\operatorname{span}_\ensuremath\mathbb{R}
\bigl\{
F(y_\nu):
\nu\in\{0,\ldots,m\}^{d}
\bigr\},$
which has dimension at most $(m+1)^{d}$.
Together with \eqref{eq:vector_chebyshev_interpolation_error}, this yields
\begin{equation}
d_{(m+1)^{d}}(\mathcal M)
\,\leq\,
C_0R^{-m}.
\label{eq:width_at_tensor_degrees}
\end{equation}

For arbitrary $n\in\ensuremath\mathbb{N}$, choose
$m_n\coloneqq\lfloor n^{1/d}\rfloor-1$.
Then $m_n\geq0$ and $(m_n+1)^{d}\leq n$.
By monotonicity of the Kolmogorov widths,
\eqref{eq:width_at_tensor_degrees}
and using
$\lfloor n^{1/d}\rfloor\geq n^{1/d}-1$,
we obtain
\[
d_n(\mathcal M)
\,\leq\,
C_0R^{-m_n}
=
C_0R^{1-\lfloor n^{1/d}\rfloor}
\,\leq\,
C_0R^2\exp\Bigl(-(\log R)n^{1/d}\Bigr).
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:generalized_exponential_width_decay}
with $\alpha_0\coloneqq C_0R^2$ and $\alpha_1\coloneqq\log R$.

title: Remark
body_md:
\label[remark]{rem:analytic_parametrization_width_decay}
The hyperrectangle assumption can be replaced by an analytic parametrization.
More precisely, suppose that $Q\subseteq\ensuremath\mathbb{R}^{\ell}$ is a compact hyperrectangle
and that $\Phi:Q\to\mathcal{P}$ is surjective.
If $\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}\circ\Phi$ admits a real-analytic extension to a neighborhood of~$Q$,
then the proof of \Cref{prop:analytic_width_decay} applies to this composition
and gives constants $\alpha_0,\alpha_1>0$, 
such that
$d_n(\mathcal M)
\,\leq\,
\alpha_0\exp\bigl(-\alpha_1 n^{1/\ell}\bigr).$

name: Analytically parametrized parameter domains

title: Corollary
head: environment
name: Convergence of the idealized greedy procedures

title: Proof
body_md:
By \Cref{prp:valid_weak_greedy} and \Cref{lem:error_equivalence_weak_greedy},
the two indicators generate weak greedy sequences with respective weakness
parameters
$\vartheta_{\mathrm{eig}}
 \coloneqq 
\sqrt{{\nu_{\min}\gamma_{\min}}/{\varrho_{\max}}}$
and 
$\vartheta_{\mathrm{aff}}
\coloneqq 
{\beta_{\min}}/{\sqrt{\varrho_{\max}}}$,
respectively.
By \Cref{prop:analytic_width_decay},
$d_n(\mathcal M)$ satisfies
\Cref{thm:weak_greedy_convergence_rates}~\ref{item:rate_decay}
with $\alpha_2=1/d$,
and the assertion follows from \Cref{thm:weak_greedy_convergence_rates}.

label: eq:discrete_training_manifold_convergence
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Convergence for a finite training set

title: Proof
body_md:
First, observe that the implementation of the active training set $\Xi_{\mathrm{act}}$ 
in \Cref{alg:greedy_reduced_basis} 
selects a maximizer over the full training set $\Xi_{\mathrm{train}}$ at every enrichment: 
once a parameter is removed from~$\Xi_{\mathrm{act}}$,
its indicator is bounded by~$\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}$ and remains so,
because the indicators are monotonically nonincreasing with~$r$.
As long as $\Xi_{\mathrm{act}}$ is nonempty, 
every active parameter has indicator value
strictly larger than~$\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}$.
Hence, the maximizer over the active set is also a maximizer over~$\Xi_{\mathrm{train}}$.

The error equivalences from \Cref{prp:valid_weak_greedy} remain valid after restricting
the parameter set to~$\Xi_{\mathrm{train}}$.
Hence, for each formulation the algorithm is a weak greedy procedure
for the finite set~$\mathcal M_\Xi$ with the corresponding weakness parameter
as given in the proof of \Cref{cor:idealized_greedy_convergence}.
Since $\mathcal M_\Xi\subseteq\mathcal M$, 
we have
$d_n(\mathcal M_\Xi)
\,\leq\,
d_n(\mathcal M)
\,\leq\,
\alpha_0\exp\bigl(-\alpha_1 n^{1/d}\bigr)$
for all $n\in\ensuremath\mathbb{N}$.
Hence, the weak greedy theorem, 
together with the fixed-initial-space argument from
\Cref{rem:fixed_initial_space_weak_greedy},
 proves \eqref{eq:discrete_training_manifold_convergence}.


For any subspace $V\subseteq\mathcal H$ and $\mu\in\mathcal{P}$, choose
$\xi\in\Xi_{\mathrm{train}}$ minimizing the state-space distance in
\eqref{eq:intrinsic_training_set_distance}.  Since the distance to a fixed
subspace is $1$-Lipschitz, we have 
\[
\mathrm{dist}\bigl(\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu),V\bigr)
\leq
\mathrm{dist}\bigl(\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\xi),V\bigr)
+
\|\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)-\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\xi)\|.
\]
If $\Xi_{\mathrm{act}}$ is empty, monotonicity of $\Delta_\star^{(r)}$ implies
\(
\max_{\xi\in\Xi_{\mathrm{train}}}
\Delta_\star^{(r)}(\xi)
\,\leq\,
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}.
\)
The reliability inequalities from \Cref{prp:valid_weak_greedy} then show that
$\sup_{\xi\in\Xi_{\mathrm{train}}}
\mathrm{dist}\bigl(\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\xi),V_{r,\star}^{\Xi}\bigr)
\,\leq\,
\sqrt{C_\star\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}}.$
This estimate and the preceding discretization argument yield 
the first inequality in \eqref{eq:finite_training_set_stopping_error}.

It remains to prove that $\delta_\Xi\leq L_uh_\Xi$.
By \Cref{prop:analyticity_steady_state_map},
$D\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}$ is continuous on the compact set~$\mathcal{P}$,
so $L_u<\infty$.
Moreover, the hyperrectangle~$\mathcal{P}$ is convex.
Hence, the line segment between $\mu$ and~$\xi$ lies in~$\mathcal{P}$, 
and the mean-value estimate gives
\(
\|
\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\mu)-\rho_{\mathrm{ss}}(\xi)
\|
\,\leq\,
L_u\|\mu-\xi\|_2.
\)
Taking the supremum proves $\delta_\Xi\leq L_u h_\Xi$,
 and hence, 
 the remaining
inequality in \eqref{eq:finite_training_set_stopping_error}.
